name: Holospace kernel
purpose: Decides every Holospace question in one proved app: whether an app is verified and may run, whether received bytes are accepted, which stored item a holospace may touch, what a guest may read, write or reach, and which lifecycle step is allowed. Send a kernel word (verdict, admission, isolation, gate or lifecycle) and that kernel's fields.
inputLabel: Request: kernel word, then its fields

promise.headline: Every Holospace decision is made by a rule Lean has proved things about.
promise.detail: Five kernels and an identity encoding, 49 theorems in all, each checked by the Lean kernel when this page was built. The proofs are about the rules; that the shell obeys an answer is tested, not proved.

claim: HK-01: An app is answered verified exactly when its seal, members, provenance and acceptance vectors all pass, and blocked otherwise. HK-02: Bytes whose hash differs from the requested name are never accepted or re-keyed, and a SHA-256 name is re-keyed only at import. HK-03: A holospace is never allowed another holospace's private state, is always allowed its own, and never writes shared content. HK-04: Nothing is allowed without a grant, a denied request is always denied, and a network request through an extension or a node is never answered allow. HK-05: Start, suspend and resume are answered only in the phase each needs, resume only with the latest snapshot, and nothing follows terminate. HK-06: The same architecture and definition digest give the same identity bytes, and a different architecture or digest always gives different ones.

proposition.name: dispatch
proposition.text:
dispatch request :=
  verdict ...   -> HolospaceLaunchVerdict.judge
  admission ... -> HolospaceAdmission.judge
  isolation ... -> HolospaceIsolation.judge
  gate ...      -> HolospaceCapabilityGate.judge
  lifecycle ... -> HolospaceLifecycle.judge
  otherwise     -> invalid
proposition.plain: The first word names the kernel, and that kernel's proved rules decide the answer.
